measurement: G ON v3 — CONFIRMED ON SEED 47. 75 independent problems, zero signatures shared with seed 21, head trained on seed-21 tasks < 226 and blind to all of these.

the_bar_on_both.OBJECTIVE >= 23.1% at no higher cost: 38.7% at 9.17 vs 10.71; 29.3% at 9.81 vs 10.68 — PASSES BOTH LIMBS ON BOTH SETS. More problems solved AND cheaper, twice.

THE_HONEST_NUANCE_THAT_MUST_TRAVEL: THE EFFECT IS SMALLER ON THE INDEPENDENT SET: +21.4 points on seed 21's held-out slice, +12.0 on seed 47. Seed 21 slice 4 was held out BY TASK INDEX from the same generator run -- adjacent tasks, same session of the grammar -- while seed 47 is a separate run sharing no signature. The 12.0 is the number to carry; the 21.4 is the number measured closer to the training distribution, and reporting their average would hide exactly that.
the_bases_replicate_almost_exactly: 13/75 = 17.3% on both, 10.71 vs 10.68 actions. Two independent draws of 75 problems from the same grammar land on the same difficulty, which is the first evidence that v3's rates are a property of the generator and not of a seed.

the_effect_is_where_the_head_disagrees_o.reading: the agreement group moves +2 and then -2, which is what a temperature confound looks like when it is noise rather than bias. The disagreement group moves +14 and +11 -- same direction, similar size, on disjoint problems.

bounds: n = 75 per set, SE 4.4-5.6. Two sets, not a sweep.
One model, one layer (18), one head, one task generator. The grammar's operation families are shared between the two seeds even though no signature is.
The head reads the post-inspect decision only, in the inspect-first loop, which is itself a hand-written change that doubled problems solved on v2.
v3's failures are localisation-bound (the budget probe: doubling the budget converts 6 of 65). On a repair-bound set the same head would be expected to do nothing -- that is what v2 measured.
